metadata.title: PHOTO-CAT: Photometric Contamination Analyzer Tool
metadata.description:
PHOTO-CAT is a catalog-driven, mission-agnostic tool for quantifying stellar flux contamination in wide-field photometric observations. High-precision photometric missions are sensitive to flux from neighboring stars, which can bias light curves, dilute transit depths, and degrade photometric precision; PHOTO-CAT screens targets for that risk directly from an astrometric catalog, before an observation is planned.

The pipeline builds a three-dimensional Euclidean representation of the sky from a user-provided catalog and indexes it with a memory-optimized KDTree for rapid neighbor searches. A streaming, CSR-style storage format with compact internal identifiers keeps memory overhead low enough to process catalogs with tens to hundreds of millions of sources. Per-target contamination is then computed from angular separations, relative fluxes, and a configurable aperture model: a top-hat, or a circular Gaussian PSF that weights each neighbor by the fraction of its flux falling inside the aperture, out to an influence radius equal to the aperture radius plus the PSF extent.

Catalog flux can optionally be converted into another photometric band before contamination is computed, either by integrating a blackbody spectrum through the band's transmission curve, which works for any mission passband including filters pulled from the SVO Filter Profile Service, or by applying a published Gaia empirical colour transformation, for the photometric systems and colour ranges those relations are calibrated on. Official transmission curves for Gaia, TESS, CHEOPS, MAUVE and the six Ariel channels ship with the package.

Outputs include per-target contaminating flux, contamination ratios, target purity, the number of neighboring sources and their angular separations, written as JSON alongside reproducibility metadata recording the package version, the query configuration, the index manifest and the explicit scope of the model. The tool runs from a graphical configurator or from a command-line interface. Results are catalog-level screening estimates, meant to support target selection and field-geometry decisions ahead of observations rather than to correct measured photometry.

The method and its application to the Ariel Mission Candidate Sample are described in G. Galletta et al. (2026), "PHOTO-CAT - Photometric Contamination Analyzer Tool: A High-Performance Framework for Photometric Contamination Assessment"; this reference is updated with its DOI once the article is published. Although developed for the Mauve satellite, PHOTO-CAT is mission-agnostic and readily applicable to TESS, PLATO, Ariel and other wide-field surveys.

metadata.title: HEV-like Endothelial Cells Drive Tertiary Lymphoid Structure Formation and Pathogenesis in Cerebral Cavernous Malformations
metadata.description:
Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs) are common vascular lesions causing seizures, intracerebral hemorrhage, and neurological deficits, yet no FDA-approved therapies exist for patients ineligible for surgery. Although CCMs arise from aberrant endothelial behavior driven by mutations in CCM genes, how mutant endothelial cells (ECs) remodel the microenvironment to influence disease progression remains less well understood. Here, we uncovered an immunopathogenic mechanism in CCMs: high endothelial venules (HEVs) and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs). Using single-cell RNA sequencing and histological analysis of human and mouse CCMs, we identified a HEV-like EC subset and confirmed TLS-like structure formation. In a 105-patient cohort, the presence of TLS-like structures was associated with increased lesion burden and a higher prevalence of subacute intracerebral hemorrhage. Endothelial-specific Ltbr deletion and pharmacologic inhibition of lymphotoxin-β receptor (LTβR) reduced CCM lesion progression in mice. These findings established that HEV-like ECs and TLS-like structures contribute to CCM pathogenesis and identified the HEV–TLS axis as an actionable target, offering a conceptual and therapeutic framework for the management of patients who are not candidates for surgery.

metadata.title: Negotiating Authenticity in TikTok Brand Storytelling: Audience Reception of User-Generated Content-Style Advertising
metadata.description: This chapter examines how TikTok audiences identify commercial intent, assess perceived authenticity, and negotiate the meanings of brand storytelling presented in a user-generated-content style. A qualitative descriptive study draws on semi-structured interviews with ten active TikTok users who discussed everyday life video stimuli and their wider platform experiences. The documented analysis organizes 220 excerpts into 50 initial codes, 21 subthemes, and ten themes, followed by an interpretation using Stuart Hall’s encoding/decoding framework. Participants identified commercial signals within videos and in surrounding comments, captions, and account histories. Authenticity depended on naturalness, honesty, personal relevance, and originality; awareness of promotion could either undermine or preserve that judgment. The final interpretation identified one dominant, six negotiated, and three oppositional readings. The findings position authenticity as a context-sensitive audience judgment rather than an automatic property of informal-looking branded content

metadata.title: EP_annotator: Annotating enhancer-promoter interactions using Hi-C and CUT&Tag data
metadata.description: EP_annotator is a bioinformatics tool for annotating enhancer–promoter (EP) interactions by integrating Hi-C chromatin interaction data with CUT&Tag histone modification signals (H3K27ac). It implements a six-step workflow that takes raw HiCUT allValidPairs files and CUT&Tag BED files as input and produces annotated EP interaction maps, supporting the mouse genome (mm10).

metadata.title: PREDICTING THE UNPREDICTABLE RAMP: PROBABILISTIC MACHINE LEARNING MODELS FOR AIRCRAFT BAGGAGE OFFLOAD AND TRANSIT TIME ESTIMATION
metadata.description: Ground handling operations at commercial airports remain one of the least predictable segments of the air transport value chain, and baggage offload and onward transit represent a particularly volatile component of the ramp process. This research article examines how probabilistic machine learning models, including Gaussian process regression, Bayesian neural networks, quantile regression forests, hidden Markov models, and survival analysis frameworks, can be applied to estimate the offload duration and downstream transit time of checked baggage from aircraft arrival to sortation, transfer, or reclaim availability. Unlike deterministic point estimate models, probabilistic approaches produce full predictive distributions that quantify the uncertainty inherent in ramp operations, allowing ground handling planners, baggage system operators, and airline operations control centers to make risk informed decisions rather than relying on single average values that routinely fail during irregular operations. The article synthesizes operational data characteristics, feature engineering strategies, and model architectures suited to the short haul, high frequency nature of ramp events. It presents an illustrative simulation study demonstrating how calibrated uncertainty intervals shrink misconnection risk and improve resource allocation for tug drivers, belt loaders, and baggage handling system capacity. The findings indicate that probabilistic models, when properly calibrated, can reduce short connection misconnection exposure, improve staffing precision during irregular operations, and provide a quantitative basis for minimum connection time policy review at hub airports.

metadata.title: Project Sovereign Genesis: The Chiral Hydro-Kinetic Matrix System CERN Engineering & Technical Manifesto (Part One)
metadata.description:
Here is the unified, comprehensive Description and Keyword Metadata for all three parts of the CERN Engineering & Technical Manifesto: The Chiral Hydro-Kinetic Matrix System (Project Genesis), formatted for immediate copy-pasting into your master catalog or Zenodo archive.
📝 Combined Project Description
The Chiral Hydro-Kinetic Matrix System (Project Genesis) is a comprehensive, three-part engineering and socioeconomic blueprint developed to replace ecologically destructive, high-maintenance hydroelectric dams with a completely decentralized, invisible, and self-stabilizing underwater energy network. Deployed flat against existing riverbeds and directly within the natural froth of waterfalls, this advanced biomimetic system operates as a three-dimensional "fluid sponge" that transforms extreme climate-driven weather, severe storms, and seasonal flood surges into a predictable source of high-voltage baseline electricity.
  • Part One: Structural, Material, and Telemetry Core details the physical architecture. Dimpled, diamond-hard ceramic loops infused with reclaimed tungsten act as an indestructible exoskeleton that completely neutralizes systemic twisting torque via an alternating 3:1 chiral reversal mechanism. Wrapped within this skeleton, flexible hydrophobic TENG blankets featuring dragonfly-wing micro-textures harvest high-voltage static electricity directly from accelerated internal water vortices. The internal telemetry runs pure, un-jammable electro-optic monitoring via the Pockels Effect inside an advanced, vacuum-sealed Carbon Nanofiber (CNF) biowire ribbon, completely eliminating internal oxidation and moisture short-circuits.
  • Part Two: Downstream Hatchery & Eco-Filtration Infrastructure integrates an active environmental engine into the grid's fluid dynamics. The system exploits the low-pressure fluid wakes generated by the matrix's counter-rotational loops to establish asymmetric, low-velocity coves. Lined with rough-cut quartz crystals, these coves act as safe, sheltered spawning sanctuaries that accelerate juvenile fish growth. Interlocking networks of carved volcanic basalt and porous sandstone triskeles run a continuous, passive water purification loop upstream and downstream of the nurseries. The sandstone filters out sediment, while the iron-rich basalt leaches vital trace minerals to balance river pH and physically block toxic blue-green algae blooms. The resulting explosion in wild fish populations drives an automated marine-derived nutrient subsidy loop, where macro-filtered fish waste is converted by microbes into bio-available liquid fertilizer that fuels explosive riverbank vegetation growth, permanently stabilizing the shorelines against climate-driven soil erosion.
  • Part Three: Global Materials Blueprint, Civil Reclamation, & Socioeconomic Labor Allocation outlines a fully circular, self-funding deployment model. Instead of relying on extractive mining, the system harvests millions of tonnes of high-purity copper and industrial tungsten straight from the turbines of obsolete, decommissioned dams to build the matrix's internal Litz 3 tracks and tungsten-ceramic weaves. The monolithic concrete walls of old dams are mechanically crushed on-site, converting structural liabilities into high-grade recycled aggregates for green urban paving and upcycled steel to frame public transit lines. This advanced material loop completely breaks the cycle of automated digital monopolies by anchoring a massive, multi-tiered employment engine directly within regional communities, distributing stable, long-term careers across advanced precision manufacturing, specialized commercial marine diving, and active optoelectronic quantum grid telemetry monitoring.

metadata.title: Reproducibility package: Old water or slow water? Transit-time distributions in tree stems and what a xylem water sample remembers
metadata.description:
Scripts, finite-element model results and data that reproduce every analysis, figure and table of the manuscript "Old water or slow water? Transit-time distributions in tree stems and what a xylem water sample remembers" (Evaristo and Johnson) and of its Supporting Information.

Study in brief. A finite-element model (COMSOL Multiphysics 6.4) of water and tracer transport in a stem is calibrated on the dye-tracer velocity profiles of Seeger and Weiler (2023), scaled to trees, and driven by the soil-water label of the 2014 Biosphere 2 deuterium-labelling experiment (Evaristo et al., 2019). A semi-analytical twin of the same stem is inverted against the canopy xylem-water curves of seven labelled trees.

What is included.

  • Java build scripts for the COMSOL API (the calibrated dye-tracer model and the tree-scale model), with the run configurations and launchers of all finite-element runs;
  • the exported results of the calibrated model (production mesh, coarse mesh, free time step) and of the 48 tree-scale runs (time series at both sampling heights, summaries, and fields for three runs); the solved .mph files are not included;
  • Python scripts for the semi-analytical stem model, the inversions and their profile-likelihood ranges, the post-processing of the finite-element runs, and every figure (PNG at 600 dpi and PDF with editable text) and table of the paper;
  • the five files of the Biosphere 2 labelling data that the analysis reads, from HydroShare (doi:10.4211/hs.60fb3a408cac40cbb38b8f559ef1fc5c, CC BY 4.0), unchanged;
  • archived copies of every computed output, a script that compares a new run with them number by number, and SHA-256 checksums of all files.

Reproduce. Python 3.11 or later; pip install -r requirements.txt, then python run_all.py --skip-inversions (all figures and tables in a few minutes) or python run_all.py (the complete analysis, inversions included, about two hours on one core), followed by python check_reproduction.py. The Python part does not need COMSOL. README.txt describes every script, the order of the steps and how to repeat the finite-element runs.

Files. The package is split into five zip archives that unpack into one folder, stem_transit_times/; extract all five into the same location. Part 1 holds the scripts, data, outputs and tables; part 2 the finite-element exports; parts 3 to 5 the field exports of three runs, which the age analysis and Figures 2, 4 and 5 read. README.txt is also provided on its own.

Scope. The package reproduces the analyses, figures and tables only; it excludes the manuscript documents and the code that typesets them. The Supplement of Seeger and Weiler (2023), from which the calibration targets are re-derived, is not redistributed: README.txt gives its DOI and checksum, and without it the archived re-derivation is used.

Licences. Scripts: MIT. Model results, derived outputs and tables: CC BY 4.0. The Biosphere 2 data remain under their own CC BY 4.0 licence (Evaristo et al., 2019).

metadata.title: Proposing a Classification Scheme for AI Usage in Scientific Articles
metadata.description:
Journals and preprint servers increasingly ask authors to disclose their use of artificial intelligence (AI), but such disclosures are almost always free text that varies from journal to journal and cannot be searched or compared. We propose AIL2026 (AI Labels), a compact, machine-readable classification of AI usage. Like the CRediT taxonomy for human contributors, it records who contributed what; like MSC2020, it uses short standardized codes, but with plain-word labels that humans can read at a glance. Each paper carries a tag: a headline level from AI-0 to AI-4 summarizing AI's role in the research itself, followed by labels stating where AI contributed and how much, each with a depth from 0 to 4. Examples are AI-0: Text1 Check2 and AI-3: Proof3 Text1. The same labels apply to every arXiv category, with field-specific interpretations. AI can contribute to research in very different ways, from light uses such as polishing text or double-checking signs and prefactors to substantial contributions such as suggesting research directions or proving theorems. We argue that light use and AI verification of any depth benefit everyone and should be encouraged: polishing makes papers easier to read, and checks with Python or Lean add a further layer of verification. Normalizing light use, which is already widespread but often undisclosed, also lowers the barrier to disclosing heavier use, since transparency, not the level of use, is what signals scientific integrity. Where AI contributes essential parts of the research, disclosure is required by good scientific practice: undisclosed use at that level confers an unfair advantage. We discuss design principles, edge cases, incentives, and a route to adoption beginning with a pilot in mathematics.

17 pages; AI usage (AIL2026): AI-3: Idea3 Result3 Proof3 Text3 Lit2 Figs3 Check2 [Claude Opus 5.5, 2026-10] (details in the section "AI usage of this paper"); MSC2020: 00A35 (primary), 68T01 (secondary)

metadata.title: The Desk Is Where You Write It Down: Why Knowledge Work Has the Wrong Model of Discovery
metadata.description:
This paper will frustrate readers who came looking for a side to take. It is not arguing for offices or against them. It is arguing that the conditions supporting discovery have been missing from much of the debate about knowledge work — and that once those conditions are named, the argument about buildings becomes a
different question.

Knowledge work includes distinguishable operations: discovering something worth pursuing and making it usable, communicable, and durable.

Discovery can emerge during focused effort, or after deliberate attention releases — on a walk, during a commute, in the shower, in an enforced pause. Cognitive psychology calls an interval of disengagement incubation; an insight that surfaces may be called illumination. Neither arrives on command. Capture — testing, recording, refining, and carrying an idea into durable form — often benefits from focused attention. The desk
is where you write it down.

metadata.title: Dataset from: Trusting the Inverse, Reliability-Aware Mapping for Simulation-Based Microstructure Estimation in Diffusion MRI
metadata.description:
CACTUS synthetic diffusion MRI dataset 

 

1050 Monte Carlo-simulated diffusion-weighted MRI signals from geometrically realistic three-dimensional white-matter substrates generated with CACTUS and simulated with MC/DC. The substrates span 7 mean axon radii (0.25–0.85 µm), 5 microscopic angular dispersions (μθ, 0–10°) and ICVF from 54% to 94%, giving 175 substrate configurations, each simulated at 6 intrinsic diffusivities (1.75–3.0 µm²/ms).

 Acquisition: PGSE with 8 diffusion times (Δ = 10–45 ms), δ = 4 ms, TE = 58 ms, b = 0–10000 s/mm² in steps of 500, and 24 gradient directions per shell: 3848 measurements per signal.

 Contents:
- signals.zip: one file per voxel and compartment (total, intra-axonal, extra-axonal), 3848 values each, big-endian float32. Signals are normalised to b = 0. The total signal is the volume-weighted average of the intra- and extra-axonal signals, with no T2 weighting.
 - properties.zip and index.csv: per-voxel properties (target mean radius, microscopic angular dispersion, target ICVF, intrinsic diffusivity, ICVF, ECVF, axon volume fraction, simulation domain size).
 - protocol.zip: the acquisition in Camino STEJSKALTANNER format (pgse.scheme) and FSL format (bvals, bvecs), plus per-measurement Δ, δ and TE.
 - README.md (file format and units), read_example.py (Python reader), SHA256SUMS (checksums).
keywords: diffusion MRI, Monte Carlo simulation, white matter, microstructure, axon radius, corpus callosum, simulation-based inference, CACTUS, MC/DC, synthetic dataset.

metadata.title: AutoTTV: automated transit-timing pipeline for TESS, v1.0.2
metadata.description: AutoTTV is an automated Bayesian pipeline for homogeneous transit-timing analysis of TESS Objects of Interest (TOIs). It fits the phase-folded light curve with an analytic transit model sampled by Markov chain Monte Carlo, measures individual mid-transit times with the transit shape held fixed, and searches the timing residuals for periodic signals, long-term period changes and excess scatter. For TTV candidates it refits the transit shape on the measured transit times, and it corrects the known timestamp errors of some QLP light curves. This release accompanies Shporer & Drori, "AutoTTV: Homogeneous Transit Timing of 3,650 TESS TOIs and the Radius Bias of Strict-Period Phase Folding" (submitted to ApJS). Version 1.0.2 refits the linear ephemeris to the remaining transits in the leave-one-out test of the scatter criterion, as in the paper's analysis.

metadata.title: TeSSHub4EOSC: FAIR training catalogue infrastructure (EOSC Symposium 2026)
metadata.description:
Lightning talk presentation at EOSC Symposium 2026. The PPTX file here labelled "embed screen" contains a screencast video in one slide; the other PPTX file also contains audio and video for the entire presentaiton. The PDF file contains no video or audio. Video is also available on YouTube.

Use the catalogue now: https://tesshub4eosc.eu/ and if you are interested in a space for your EOSC node or community, please contact us on phil.reed@manchester.ac.uk

Abstract

Training resources across the European Open Science Cloud remain fragmented, scattered across research infrastructures, universities, and domain-specific communities, making it difficult for researchers to discover relevant learning opportunities. The EOSC Gravity-funded TeSSHub4EOSC project addresses this gap by delivering a distributed, FAIR-compliant catalogue infrastructure that acts as a central training metadata backbone for the EOSC Catalogue.

Built on the mTeSS-X platform (itself an evolution of the established TeSS system, developed within the OSCARS Open Science project) TeSSHub4EOSC automates the harvesting, standardisation, and exposure of training metadata from diverse sources. The result is a single, interoperable access point that complements discipline-specific catalogues such as ELIXIR TeSS and PaN-Training, rather than replacing them. Crucially, the platform allows EOSC nodes, science clusters, and competence centres to spin up their own custom-branded "spaces" – each with distinct branding and content – without the burden of maintaining separate infrastructure.

This lightning talk showcases the outcomes of the EOSC Gravity-funded TeSSHub4EOSC project, led by HZDR and the University of Manchester in partnership with the EOSC Nodes PaNOSC and Life Sciences Connect. We will present the deployed central TeSSHub instance, its integration with EOSC-AAI for authentication, and the pilot onboarding of the service into existing EOSC Nodes, demonstrating a concrete, working example of federation in practice.

Value for EOSC: TeSSHub4EOSC directly strengthens the EOSC Federation by lowering the technical barrier for nodes and communities to expose their training offerings through a shared, standardised, machine-readable interface. It provides a possible future option that advances EOSC's strategic objectives around FAIRness, interoperability, and sustainable service federation, while reducing duplicated infrastructure effort across the landscape. By feeding curated, standardised metadata into the EOSC Catalogue and supporting the EOSC Academy, the project contributes a suggested reusable building block for scalable, community-driven training discovery; a capability currently missing at federation scale.

We will succinctly share lessons from the pilot deployment, the open-source architecture that enables incremental adoption by future nodes, and our roadmap for embedding TeSSHub as a long-term, community-governed service within the EOSC operational framework. Attendees will leave with a clear picture of how to onboard their own training catalogues, and how a shared registry model can be replicated across other thematic areas of the Federation.

metadata.title: EXTREME RESEARCH MONOGRAPH  Longevity Biomarkers Microrobotic Sampling and Trustworthy Biosensing at the Limit
metadata.description:
EXTREME RESEARCH MONOGRAPH

Longevity Biomarkers Microrobotic Sampling and Trustworthy Biosensing at the Limit

English Introduction and Publication Abstract

Research coupling

Longevity biomarkers × microrobotic sampling × trustworthy biosensing

Evidence firewall

Level 1 sample fidelity → Level 2 aging mechanism validity → Level 3 meaningful health outcome prediction

Book architecture

750 pages | 219,119 extracted English words | 82 chapters | 410 research sections | 30 linked derivations | 200 Research Gates

Scientific status

Prospective non clinical research architecture with explicit uncertainty abstention and stop boundaries

Publication Abstract

This research monograph develops a falsifiable architecture for measuring dynamic longevity biomarkers without allowing the act of sampling, transport, storage, sensing, calibration, or computation to manufacture the apparent biology. Its central premise is simple but demanding: a biomarker has scientific value only when the sample remains traceable, the measurement remains calibrated, the proposed aging mechanism survives competing explanations, and the released result retains an uncertainty boundary appropriate to its intended use.

Microrobotic sampling is treated as a candidate laboratory capability rather than an assumed improvement. The reference domain is closed microfluidics, organ on chip systems, bench top modules, authorized ex vivo samples, and separately governed prospective research. A successful robot trajectory does not establish preserved biology. Greater analytical sensitivity does not establish mechanism specificity. A younger biological age score does not establish that an intervention improves healthspan or survival.

The Three Level Evidence Firewall

Level 1 Measurement Science. Demonstrate that collection, motion, contact, field exposure, storage, preprocessing, and sensing do not alter the target state beyond a preregistered budget. Preserve sample identity, mass balance, raw evidence, calibration ancestry, and covariance aware uncertainty.

Level 2 Aging Biology. Demonstrate that the biomarker reflects a specified aging mechanism rather than tissue composition, acute stress, disease, medication, circadian state, matrix interference, batch effects, or platform drift. Require orthogonal assays and mechanism specific perturbations.

Level 3 Longevity Intervention Research. Test whether biomarker change predicts or mediates meaningful function, healthspan, morbidity, or mortality. Association is not intervention benefit. Changing a score cannot be equated with changing health without independent prospective evidence.

Candidate Research Expression

Qvalid = Pintact × Ptrace × Pmechanism × Poutcome − Dsample − Uchain − Bintervention

The expression is a research ledger rather than a universal biological law. Each probability must be estimated within a declared sample matrix, platform, population, time horizon, and claim level. Sample damage, chain uncertainty, unauthorized use, and irreversible harm are veto conditions; they cannot be compensated by an attractive aggregate score.

Five Layer Research Architecture

Sample Truth and Claim Contract. Defines specimen identity, permitted use, exposure limits, claim level, strong comparator, vetoes, exclusions, and abstention.

Microrobotic Physics and Preanalytics. Measures flow, diffusion, wall effects, adhesion, shear, heat, field exposure, contact, dead volume, recovery, storage, and matrix change.

Aging Mechanism Validation. Separates mechanism specific biology from disease, cell mixture, tissue discordance, acute physiology, circular composite construction, and attractive but noncausal narratives.

Metrology and Longitudinal Inference. Binds raw signals, calibration functions, reference ancestry, detection limits, covariance, drift, personal baselines, irregular time series, and transportability.

Outcomes Governance and Successor Control. Requires meaningful outcomes, harms, consent, privacy, subgroup calibration, portability, negative result preservation, independent reconstruction, and the right to retire the system.

Minimum Verifiable Prototype

A blinded study divides matched biological reference material into three arms: candidate microrobotic sampling, a strong manual or passive microfluidic comparator, and a time matched unhandled control where feasible. The study records device motion, force, flow, temperature, contact time, surface history, sample recovery, raw detector output, preprocessing, calibration, uncertainty, and every rejected event. A hidden disturbance such as a coating lot change, dwell time extension, temperature excursion, or reference offset is introduced. The system must detect the invalidity, preserve the failure state, and abstain before the result is promoted.

Only after sample fidelity is demonstrated does the program test whether the selected biomarker responds to a mechanism specific perturbation. Only after mechanism validity is established does a separate prospective study ask whether the marker adds calibrated information about function, disease, healthspan, or survival beyond chronological age and established clinical measures.

Research Contributions

• A three level evidence firewall that prevents sampling feasibility from becoming an aging mechanism claim or clinical conclusion.
• Thirty mathematical and physical derivations connected to chapter corridors, experiments, failure tests, and Research Gates.
• Eighty two chapters covering sample truth, microfluidic physics, preanalytics, aging biology, biosensor metrology, longitudinal models, interventions, and governance.
• Two hundred detailed Research Gates designed as future research entry points with baselines, required evidence, competing explanations, stop conditions, and successor packets.
• A lifecycle design in which manual methods, passive fluidics, classical sensors, or the retirement of a popular biomarker can legitimately defeat the more complex system.

Central Scientific Boundary

This work does not claim that microrobots currently provide autonomous human body sampling, diagnosis, therapy, or life extension. It does not treat every age associated signal as a causal hallmark, and it does not recommend personal medical action. Clinical translation would require independent analytical validation, ethical review, regulatory authorization, clinical performance studies, harm monitoring, and post deployment surveillance.

Selected DOI Research Ancestry

Hallmarks of aging an expanding universe. 10.1016/j.cell.2022.11.001

An epigenetic clock analysis of human tissues and cell types. 10.1186/gb-2013-14-10-r115

An epigenetic biomarker of aging for lifespan and healthspan. 10.18632/aging.101414

DNA methylation GrimAge strongly predicts lifespan and healthspan. 10.18632/aging.101684

DunedinPACE a DNA methylation biomarker of the pace of aging. 10.7554/eLife.73420

Mobile microrobots for bioengineering applications. 10.1039/C7LC00064B

Biologic tissue sampling with untethered microgrippers. 10.1053/j.gastro.2013.01.066

Ionic shape morphing microrobotic end effectors for sampling. 10.1038/s41467-020-20697-w

Micro invasive membrane free biochemical sampling. 10.1126/sciadv.abb0657

Uncertainty and limit of detection in label free biosensors. 10.3390/s18072038

Measurement uncertainty and metrological traceability. 10.11613/BM.2021.010501

Performance criteria for combined uncertainty budgets. 10.1515/cclm-2014-1240

Suggested English Description

Longevity Biomarkers, Microrobotic Sampling and Trustworthy Biosensing at the Limit is a 200,000 word class research monograph on the evidence required to measure biological aging without corrupting the sample or overstating the result. Across eighty two chapters, thirty linked derivations, and two hundred Research Gates, it integrates microscale transport, sample preservation, preanalytical control, aging biology, metrological traceability, longitudinal inference, intervention studies, and successor governance. The book enforces a strict three level firewall: preserved measurement must be demonstrated before mechanism validity, and mechanism validity before meaningful health outcome prediction. Its purpose is not to promise life extension, but to make future longevity research more testable, reconstructable, and capable of saying no.

Keywords

longevity biomarkers; biological aging; microrobotic sampling; microfluidics; trustworthy biosensing; metrological traceability; measurement uncertainty; epigenetic clocks; aging hallmarks; longitudinal biomarkers; healthspan; sample integrity; Research Gates

metadata.title: Flight Test Instrumentation and Data Analysis for Separating Triboelectric and Exogenous Charging in Severe Precipitation Static Environments
metadata.description: For certification, large transport aircraft must be tested in adverse weather conditions where precipitation impacts the forward surfaces, potentially generating electrostatic discharges that can interfere with communication and navigation systems. Flight testing within the defined “severe” precipitation environment often requires multiple flights without a comprehensive understanding and interpretation of the resulting flight test data. This paper provides new insights into the airplane charging environment by distinguishing between triboelectric charging and exogenous airplane-level charging conditions using data from onboard instrumentation. These insights can be used classify flight test data in as gathered during “severe” charging conditions during system functionality verification. The authors aim to complement the verification methods for p-static protection effectiveness described in ARP5672.

metadata.title: TRANSLATING BEYOND WORDS: PARALINGUISTIC CHALLENGES IN MACHINE TRANSLATION AND AUDIOVISUAL TRANSLATION
metadata.description: Translation is not limited to transferring words and grammatical structures from one language into another, because communication also depends on voice, emotion, intonation, pauses, gestures, facial expressions, and other paralinguistic signals. This article examines the main difficulties that arise when such information is transferred through machine translation and audiovisual translation. Particular attention is given to stress, intonation, tone of voice, hesitation, laughter, sarcasm, gestures, and culturally specific visual signals. The study uses a qualitative comparative approach and analyzes representative examples in order to identify how communicative meaning may be weakened or lost during automated translation. The discussion shows that a translation can be lexically and grammatically correct while still failing to reproduce the speaker’s emotional attitude or communicative intention. The article therefore argues that future translation technologies should treat paralinguistic information as an important part of meaning rather than as secondary information.

A lightweight online assessment system for university mathematics and physics courses, built on Google Apps Script and Google Sheets with a single-page web client. The system records basic behavioural signals during the test to support academic integrity, and is designed to run on free infrastructure for groups of about 30–80 students.

metadata.title: Archival eclipses support a close stellar companion of TYC 6355-1082-1
metadata.description:
Archival eclipses support a close stellar companion of TYC 6355-1082-1

Friedrich Otto Krone
Independent researcher, Germany
ORCID: https://orcid.org/0009-0009-5733-2966
Observational analysis: 11 October 2026; publication preparation: 16 October 2026

TYC 6355-1082-1, TIC 415683911, Gaia DR3 6832597767349625984 is a previously
catalogued star. Three independent observing programmes, TESS, SuperWASP and ZTF,
show alternating primary and secondary eclipses. Their different depths support
a full orbital period near 5.0151 days, rather than the half-period alias. A close
stellar binary interpretation is strongly supported, but worldwide priority and
a dynamical companion mass are not established.

Gaia DR3 epoch-2016 coordinates are RA 318.91450486442096 degrees and
Dec -20.233344363000175 degrees; G = 12.0242 mag. The parallax is
2.56574 +/- 0.02262 mas. TESS sector 92 contains 9,942 quality-selected QLP
measurements and four fully covered primary and secondary eclipses. Depths are
approximately 5.80 and 3.87 percent; full durations are near 2.95 and 2.93 hours.
TARS re-reduction of the same TESS photons is a sensitivity check, not another
instrument. Its independently published rotation catalogue already includes
this known variable at 5.2626 days; that value is not the eclipse orbital period.

SuperWASP provides 10,099 original observations, of which 8,763 pass the
documented selection. Its independently fitted period is 5.0151748 +/-
0.0000301 days, with formal errors. Corrected and uncorrected series reproduce
the eclipse morphology; FLAG 32 denotes TAMUZ correction rather than a generic
bad-quality flag. The ZTF-only fit gives 5.0150754 +/- 0.0000262 days, with formal
errors. A joint constant-period descriptive fit gives 5.0150987 days and primary
epoch BJD_TDB 2460805.517458. Its nominal precision excludes correlated errors
and model uncertainty and is not a guarantee of long-term phase prediction.

Primary and secondary TESS difference-image centres lie 0.114 and 0.120 pixels
from the target's catalogue position. Bootstrap statistics do not include full
WCS/PSF systematics; these offsets do not prove subarcsecond localization.
Known Gaia neighbours are too faint to explain the entire optical light loss.
An unresolved multiple-star configuration is not universally excluded.
Gaia independently reports 30 RV transits over 886.7 days and a robust full RV
range of 134.42 km/s. Public individual RVs and a phase-resolved spectroscopic
orbit were not located; no orbital RV semiamplitude or dynamical mass is claimed.

NEOWISE gives additional sparse phase-dependent support. ASAS, NSVS, Catalina,
DASCH, APPLAUSE, AllWISE and Pan-STARRS have weak or inadequate eclipse coverage
and are not counted as secure extra confirmations. The German six-page report
documents those negative and unavailable tests, timing conventions and limits.
The model of two luminous spheres is descriptive and does not uniquely determine
component radii or temperatures for the grazing eclipses.

Earlier searches covered source-linked SIMBAD information, positional VSX and
TESS-EB queries, Gaia/SB9/WDS, ExoFOP, 110 VizieR catalogues, the full Schanche
SuperWASP table, the Liu et al. 2026 TESS-EB table and Penev 2026 data/code tables.
They found no prior matching close-binary interpretation. The recorded 14 October 2026 VSX
query also returns no objects in a 2-arcminute cone around the target. These are
finite searches and cannot prove worldwide priority. The new contribution is
the supported eclipsing-binary interpretation and full period of a known star,
not the first observation of the star or the first detection of variability.

Data and code: the curated package preserves the original measurements,
exposure/cadence time corrections, source and neighbour checks, known-object
tests, analysis scripts, original provenance links and a SHA-256 inventory.
The source archive's per-file hashes were verified before repackaging. This is
archive-integrity verification; no fresh independent re-execution of all the
historical analyses is claimed in this packaging step.

Data producers retain attribution and their original terms: NASA TESS/MAST,
MIT QLP, TARS, the WASP consortium/CERIT-SC, ZTF/IRSA, ESA Gaia/DPAC, ASAS,
NSVS, Catalina, DASCH, APPLAUSE, Pan-STARRS, CDS and AAVSO. Third-party journal
PDFs and full journal article texts are excluded. Original observations were
not acquired by the analysing author. Author-created text and analysis code
are offered under CC BY 4.0; this does not override upstream data/code terms.
OpenAI Codex assisted data retrieval, analysis code, verification, plots and
drafting. No synthetic astronomical observations were generated. The human
author is responsible for the scientific content.

metadata.title: Archival eclipses identify a close stellar companion of HD 202634
metadata.description:
A research note identifying a strongly supported close eclipsing stellar companion of the known star HD 202634 (TIC 415685424; Gaia DR3 6832999436987793408). TESS, independently acquired NEOWISE, ASAS and NSVS photometry, and Gaia radial-velocity variability support a period near 2.4703 days. A further fixed-ephemeris test detects the primary eclipse in 1,262 quality-selected Harvard DASCH photographic measurements from 1900 to 1949.

metadata.title: A Case Study on the Performance Metrics of Integrated Photonic Computing
metadata.description: Photonic processors use optical signals for computation, leveraging the high bandwidth and low loss of optical links. While many approaches have been proposed, including in memory photonic circuits, most efforts have focused on the physical design of photonic components rather than full architectural integration with electronic peripheral circuitry. In this work, we present a microarchitecture level study that estimates the compute efficiency and density of three prominent photonic computing architectures. Our evaluation accounts for both the photonic circuits and the essential peripheral electronics required for optoelectronic and analog to digital conversions. We further demonstrate a heterogenous photonic electronic in memory processing approach for low latency neural network inference. These results provide a better understanding of the design aspects of photonic computing.

metadata.title: MyoCyter v2.0.49: An ImageJ/Fiji Macro for Cardiomyocyte Contractility Analysis (Software and User Manual)
metadata.description:
MyoCyter v2.0.49 – ImageJ/Fiji Macro for Cardiomyocyte Contractility Analysis

MyoCyter v2.0.49 is an open-source macro for ImageJ/Fiji developed for the quantitative analysis of contractile activity in cardiomyocytes and other contracting cells using high-frame-rate microscopy videos.

The software extracts motion-related signals from differences between consecutive video frames and from differences relative to a reference frame. Based on these signals, MyoCyter calculates a comprehensive set of parameters describing individual contraction cycles, including contraction and relaxation times, movement amplitudes, peak timing, threshold-dependent kinetics, and beat-to-beat variability.

Version 2.0 extends the original MyoCyter workflow with integrated multi-cell analysis, assisted manual region-of-interest (ROI) selection, reproducible ROI manifests, batch processing, quality-control and exclusion procedures, and re-evaluation of previously extracted data.

Additional functionality includes:

  • Automated extraction of contraction-level and cell-level results

  • Statistical aggregation and comparison across samples and experiments

  • Data preparation for downstream statistical analysis

  • Integrated statistical procedures, including two-group comparisons and ANOVA workflows

  • Visualization of contraction kinetics using plots, heatmaps, scatterplots, and comparative maps

  • Standardized export of numerical results and graphical outputs

The software is designed to preserve the hierarchical organization of experimental data, including individual contractions, cells, and experimental groups. Statistical analyses must account for the underlying experimental design and the non-independence of repeated contractions and cells originating from the same biological sample.

Files included in this release

  1. MyoCyter v2.0.49 – complete ImageJ macro source code.

  2. MyoCyter v2.0 – user manual describing software installation, data preparation, analysis procedures, and interpretation of the results.

Software requirements

MyoCyter requires ImageJ (version 1.52p or later) or a compatible Fiji installation. The software was developed and tested primarily under Windows. Input videos must be provided in an AVI format compatible with ImageJ/Fiji. High-frame-rate recordings (preferably at least 120 frames per second) are recommended for reliable characterization of rapid cardiomyocyte contractions.

Related publication

Jung, T. (2026). MyoCyter v2.0: an open-source ImageJ macro for cardiomyocyte contractility analysis. Research Square, preprint. https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-10189255/v1

https://github.com/Myocyter/MyoCyter-v2.0

MyoCyter is intended for scientific research and educational use. Results generated by the software should be independently reviewed and interpreted in the context of the experimental design.

metadata.title: Floor Perturbations in the ZR Framework for Big Health data: A Technical Note
metadata.description:
Abstract

This technical note clarifies the algebraic mechanics and stress-testing rationale of the ZR framework we recently proposed for massive healthcare datasets (i.e., big health data). By eliminating population denominator scaling, ZR isolates raw event count dynamics. We here formalize how fine-grained ( less than 1%) lower-bound perturbations act as an engineering diagnostic to evaluate the structural stability of rare-event epidemiological signals near critical inferential limits.

metadata.title: Machine Learning Approaches for Ionospheric Scintillation Analysis Using ScintPi Observations
metadata.description: Ionospheric scintillation refers to rapid phase and amplitude fluctuations of radio signals as they pass through ionospheric irregularities. While commercial scintillation monitors have been used extensively to study scin- tillation, their relatively high costs have limited scientific use. To address this, we have been developing low- cost scintillation monitors based on single-board computers and Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers. These instruments, referred to as ScintPi, have been deployed at different locations over the globe, producing a very large and valuable dataset which has motivated the development of data-driven processing and analysis techniques. This work presents a two-stage machine learning (ML) framework applied to scintillation measurements made by ScintPi monitors. More specifically, the framework consists of: (1) a supervised classification to automat- ically identify scintillation in GNSS data, and (2) a supervised regression to infer scintillation severity from Total Electron Content (TEC) measurements. In the first stage, the goal is to distinguish true ionospheric scintillation from non-geophysical disturbances such as multipath and radio frequency interference (RFI). Supervised classification models were trained using a labeled dataset with known disturbance sources: multipath, RFI, or low-latitude scintillation. Features were derived from signal power spectra and TEC. Preliminary results show that tree-based models can distinguish scintillation from multipath and RFI with approximately 99% classification accuracy. These results were used to generate a cleaned dataset of approximately 1,100,000 low-latitude, quiet-time scintillation observations during 2024. In the second stage, the goal is to use the cleaned dataset from the first stage to interpret the Rate of Change of TEC Index (ROTI) derived from lower-rate GNSS observations. While ROTI is expected to be correlated with the amplitude scintillation index S4, the relationship between these two variables depends on many factors including link geometry, irregularity drift, and irregularity spectrum. Determining a relationship between S4 and ROTI is important since it could allow estimates of scintillation severity from the wide network of geodetic receivers rather than specialized scintillation monitors alone. Supervised regression models were trained to infer S4 from ROTI. Features include ROTI from 1 Hz TEC, link geometry, local time, and solar activity. Model performance was evaluated using an independent low-latitude station outside the longitude sector used for training. Preliminary results show strong agreement between estimated and observed S4 (Pearson r ~ 0.92). Overall, the results demonstrate the usefulness of ML techniques to aid processing of scintillation measure- ments and to relate scintillation parameters to different types of observations (e.g., ROTI).
